candidates.title: Periphery designs its own mobility standard
candidates.shift: Kathmandu Valley is assessing an integrated green urban transport system largely unconstrained by legacy car infrastructure, potentially leapfrogging Western auto-centric planning norms.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: feasibility studies in car-light, high-growth peripheral cities could yield mobility/zoning templates retailers elsewhere later borrow. Strange because it's still an academic study, not policy.
candidates.evidence: Paper assesses integrated green urban transport for Kathmandu Valley, citing congestion, degraded pedestrian infrastructure, and unplanned road expansion.
candidates.initial_analysis: A shift from car-dependent to integrated multimodal transit planning in a peripheral high-growth valley; if adopted, could reshape retail site accessibility and street-frontage standards without a car-centric legacy to unwind.
candidates.author: Surakshya Basnet, Namaraj Lamichhane, Nishma Rajan Magar et al.

candidates.title: Pharma-grade cold chain standards spilling toward retail cold storage
candidates.shift: Advances in Good Distribution Practice and cold-chain integrity monitoring for biologics could set a technical bar that grocery/retail cold storage and receiving eventually gets held to.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative and a stretch: pharma-grade traceability tech (loggers, GDP audits) may become the reference standard retailers borrow for perishable receiving/storage compliance and insurance.
candidates.evidence: Paper reviews GDP-governed cold chain integrity methods for temperature-sensitive pharmaceuticals amid market growth.
candidates.source: International Journal of Health and Pharmaceutical Research
candidates.initial_analysis: A shift from ad hoc cold storage monitoring toward pharma-grade traceability infrastructure; if it crosses into grocery retail, receiving docks and backroom storage would need new sensor and compliance investment.
candidates.author: Oluchi Beatrice Aneke

candidates.title: Removing ink becomes the bottleneck for circular packaging
candidates.shift: New surfactant-based deinking methods for post-consumer polyethylene aim to make recycled film transparent and high-quality enough for demanding reuse, closing a material-science gap in circular packaging.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: niche materials science, but it addresses an absence (no scalable deinking standard) that retail packaging circularity commitments quietly depend on.
candidates.evidence: Preprint investigates industrially applicable surfactants for deinking PE post-consumer waste flakes for high-quality recyclates.
candidates.initial_analysis: A shift from downcycled opaque plastics to viable transparent recycled film; if scaled, retailers' circular-packaging commitments become technically achievable rather than aspirational marketing claims.
candidates.author: Steven Zimmer, Lisa Leuchtenberger-Engel, Achim Grefenstein et al.

candidates.title: Adaptive triage for what happens after a product's store life ends
candidates.shift: A new adaptive multi-stage model for deciding end-of-life product recovery pathways (resale, repair, recycle) responds to the absence of dynamic, condition-based sorting systems.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: points toward a coming category — automated, condition-based triage infrastructure for returns and end-of-life goods that stores and reverse-logistics hubs currently lack.
candidates.evidence: Journal of Manufacturing Systems paper proposes an adaptive multi-stage model for EoL product recovery given variable condition and residual value.
candidates.initial_analysis: A shift from static, one-size sorting of returned/end-of-life goods to adaptive, condition-based triage; if adopted, requires new backroom or DC infrastructure and roles dedicated to real-time recovery-pathway decisions.
candidates.author: Youxi Hu, Lve Sun, Richard Fox et al.

candidates.title: A material passport for store fit-outs that don't want to be permanent
candidates.shift: A proposed 'reversible decoration' framework tracks materials through indoor renovation cycles via a digital material cycle map, addressing the absence of traceability for reused fit-out materials.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: retail stores refresh every 3-5 years; a digital material passport for shelving/fixtures could turn renovation waste into a tracked circular asset class.
candidates.evidence: Study proposes a Digital Material Cycle Map (DMCM) supporting tracking, recovery and reuse of construction materials in indoor renovation projects.
candidates.initial_analysis: A shift from disposable store fit-out cycles toward trackable, reusable material systems; if standardized, store renovation contracts and construction-waste accounting would need new material-passport data fields.
candidates.author: R. Wang
